arguments.help: R4.7: enable autoscaling between MIN..MAX workers based on queue depth. Scale-up when pending tasks exceed 50 * active workers; scale-down after 60s of sustained idle. 30s cooldown between decisions. Implies --processes (the initial count is clamped into [MIN,MAX]).
arguments.name: --autoscale

arguments.help: Burst mode (R4.5): exit cleanly once all configured queues have been idle for --burst-idle-timeout seconds. Useful for batch / cron-style deployments where a worker should drain and exit rather than long-poll forever.
arguments.name: --burst

arguments.help: Seconds of queue silence required before --burst exits (default: 5.0). The idle clock starts at worker-ready and resets on every delivered message. Ignored without --burst. Exit code 0 on clean drain (indistinguishable from SIGTERM; grep logs for 'burst_idle_exit' to distinguish).
arguments.name: --burst-idle-timeout

arguments.help: Dry-run validation mode. Verify --module is importable, (with --reload) that 'watchfiles' is installed + watch-dirs resolve, and that multi-process mode is not combined with a fixed --metrics-port/--health-port. Prints a JSON summary to stdout, exits 0 on success or 1 on any validation error. Does NOT connect to broker or backend.
arguments.name: --check

arguments.help: Maximum tasks executed in parallel (default: 10). With --pool cpu this is the number of compute slots; the default is then the number of CPUs assigned to the worker (affinity and cgroup quota), divided by --processes.
arguments.name: --concurrency

arguments.help: R5.2: serve /health + /ready on the given port. /ready pings broker + backend (2s timeout) and returns structured JSON. Default bind: 127.0.0.1.
arguments.name: --health-port

arguments.help: Log output format (default: human). 'json' for agent/log-aggregator consumption.
arguments.name: --log-format

arguments.help: Log verbosity (default: INFO). DEBUG also surfaces full tracebacks on CLI errors.
arguments.name: --log-level

arguments.help: R5.1: serve Prometheus /metrics on the given port. Auto-wires the signal-based collectors (task_total, retries_total, etc.). Requires 'pip install swarmq[metrics]'. Default bind: 127.0.0.1.
arguments.name: --metrics-port

arguments.help: Python module containing Task subclasses to register, e.g. 'myapp.tasks'. Must be importable from the current Python path.
arguments.name: --module

arguments.help: Execution pool (default: io). 'cpu' runs every task body in a compute child forked from a pre-warmed forkserver: the loop process never computes, hard_timeout and cancel kill the child, --concurrency means compute slots. POSIX only; not combinable with --autoscale.
arguments.name: --pool

arguments.help: R4.3: auto-declare + consume the high/normal/low triplet for every --queues base queue, so tasks with TaskInfo(priority='high'|'low') route correctly. Without this flag, priority-tagged tasks publish to {queue}.high/.low which are never consumed.
arguments.name: --priorities

arguments.help: R4.6: run N worker subprocesses under a supervisor (ProcessManager). Default 1 keeps the legacy in-process behaviour. Subprocesses use multiprocessing spawn — fresh broker/backend connections per worker. The supervisor auto-restarts crashed workers (max 5 restarts per hour), and reloads on SIGHUP via os.execvp().
arguments.name: --processes

arguments.help: Comma-separated queue names to consume from (default: default).
arguments.name: --queues

arguments.help: R5.3: watch task modules for changes and trigger the existing SIGHUP reload pipeline (ProcessManager execvp). Implies --processes (activates the supervisor when no --processes/--autoscale is passed). Developer-only — do not use in production. Requires 'pip install "swarmq[reload]"'. Missing dep exits with code 1; invalid --watch-dir exits 2.
arguments.name: --reload

arguments.help: R5.3: directory to watch (repeatable). Without this flag, the parent directory of --module's resolved source file is used. Ignored without --reload (a WARNING is logged).
arguments.name: --watch-dir

commands.help: Import a Python module so its Task subclasses register, then connect to broker + backend and consume. Broker and backend URLs come from SWARMQ_BROKER_URL and SWARMQ_BACKEND_URL environment variables. Note: importing the module runs its top-level code — this is the standard Python convention.
